key_insight: Identical behavior can hide different integrated information, while finite experiments can certify mechanism-level lower bounds when access and uncertainty are carefully controlled.
engineering_relevance: AI audits targeting internal mechanisms should design interventions for identifiability rather than rely on input-output agreement or near-perfect surrogate fits.
method: Analyze identifiability and continuity of integrated information φ in stochastic four- and five-unit networks.
Compare behavioral, partial-recording and interventional access against known ground truth.
Construct robust lower bounds and finite-data certificates with controlled false-certificate probability.
evidence_signal: Behaviorally identical networks had φ values of 0.28 and 0 bits; internal recordings distinguished them in 4–53 trials, and about 10^7 controlled transitions certified φ > 1.004 bits over a 64-dimensional mechanism region.
watch_item: Results concern small networks; hidden units and discontinuities can defeat precise estimation even with abundant data or highly accurate surrogate models.
paper_title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
